why: Universes at 0. A states the clauses for a basic strong bundle construction Bs and its chosen representative Bs.rep (Ψ ranging over the uniformizers of toE); B states them for arbitrary bundle transition data F̄ of a strong bundle uniformizer construction, with the topology generated by the printed collection. Every F̄ is a representative of the construction ⟨Fb, ⟦F̄⟧⟩, equivalent to its rep, and equivalent data give the same topologies on M(Ψ̄, Ψ̄') and on M(Ψ, Ψ') (non-item isOpenTr_of_equiv, toETD_equiv); B's generated topology has exactly the printed open sets. So every clause transfers along identity homeomorphisms, and the statements are the same. theorem_19_6_11_four (ι) is a def, hence vocabulary rather than a conjunct of A: in A_to_B the ι clause of B, and the clause 'the open sets are exactly T̄', are proved without A (TransitionData.invHomeomorph, the generated-topology glue); all other clauses use A.
